sentences.text: The genus Archaeolamna includes three valid species, with one containing two subspecies, found across Europe, North America, and Australia.
It stands as the only surviving member of the family Archaeolamnidae after other related genera were reassigned or synonymized.
A 2026 study using enameloid zinc isotope values suggests that Archaeolamna occupied high trophic positions in the Late Cretaceous Western Interior Seaway.
These sharks lived from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 113.2 and 66 million years ago.
They likely had an antitropical distribution, inhabiting temperate waters in both hemispheres but avoiding tropical waters near the equator.
